00314.title: Cisplatin + fluorouracil · 28-day cycle
00314.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic head and neck cancer under NCCP 00314; confirm the individual treatment aim and relationship to any separately planned local treatment.
00314.purpose: Cisplatin and fluorouracil are used to treat head and neck cancer. The treatment aim depends on the extent of the cancer and your wider plan; ask your team to record whether the aim is disease control, symptom relief or part of another treatment strategy.
00314.schedule: Both medicines are given on Days 1–4 of each 28-day cycle. Treatment continues while appropriate, until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable; this protocol does not set a fixed number of cycles.
material_risks: Serious infection or bleeding from low blood counts
Kidney injury, electrolyte disturbance, hearing loss and nerve damage
Nausea/vomiting, mouth/bowel inflammation and dehydration
Fluorouracil cardiac or early excessive toxicity; hand-foot syndrome
Infusion allergy and reproductive/fertility effects
00314.discussion: Discuss intended benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or lasting harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Confirm the exact indication and current licensed/off-label position.
limitations: Historical advanced-disease comparison; not evidence of curative benefit or the exact current schedule.
Response, survival and treatment-related harm are different outcomes; cross-trial comparisons do not rank current alternatives.
support: Prescribe regimen-specific hydration and electrolyte replacement with fluid-balance review. The appropriate volume depends on kidney and cardiac status; a generic printed plan is not an intravenous-fluid prescription.
Review hearing, tinnitus and peripheral nerve symptoms before each cycle; damage can persist. Review nephrotoxic, ototoxic and other interacting medicines.

Record the DPD result before the first fluorouracil exposure unless previously tested. Complete deficiency precludes fluorouracil; partial deficiency needs an individual starting dose and careful subsequent review.
Normal DPD testing cannot exclude all severe fluorouracil toxicity. Explain unexpectedly early or severe diarrhoea, mucositis, neurological symptoms and chest pain.
Write the actual infusion option, access arrangement, bag or pump changes and disconnect time. Do not equate four treatment days with a single universal pump duration.
Provide an individually prescribed diarrhoea plan and hand/foot care advice; severe or persistent symptoms require assessment rather than repeated self-treatment.
Arrange nutrition, weight and swallowing review early. Dietitian and speech and language therapy input should follow the person’s needs; swallowing safety cannot be inferred from a general leaflet.
Use the agreed mouth-care and dental plan. Report painful swallowing, mouth ulceration, weight loss or inability to drink before the next appointment.
Reconcile prescription, over-the-counter and complementary medicines. Discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding using the actual products and individual circumstances.
Confirm the hospital’s urgent contact and fever instructions. Infection, bleeding, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, chest pain or new breathlessness need prompt assessment, not the next routine review.

00552.title: Carboplatin + fluorouracil after chemoradiotherapy · nasopharyngeal cancer
00552.setting: Adjuvant chemotherapy after chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced stage III or IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma when cisplatin is contraindicated or not tolerated.
00552.purpose: This chemotherapy is an additional treatment after chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal cancer. It aims to treat cancer cells that may remain. The team explains the expected benefit and burden for you, including recovery from the earlier treatment.
00552.schedule: After recovery, adjuvant chemotherapy is planned to begin 4 weeks after completion of weekly carboplatin with radiotherapy (NCCP 00419). Carboplatin is given on Day 1 and fluorouracil over Days 1–4, every 28 days for up to 3 cycles. The treating team confirms readiness and dates.
material_risks: Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Nausea/vomiting, mouth/throat inflammation, diarrhoea and dehydration
Fluorouracil cardiac/early excessive toxicity and hand-foot syndrome
Platinum allergy, hearing and nerve effects
Nutritional deterioration after chemoradiotherapy; reproductive/fertility effects
00552.discussion: Discuss intended benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or lasting harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Explain and document the off-label indication/combination and current licensing position under local policy.
limitations: As-treated analysis, single-centre design and a combined concurrent/adjuvant intervention limit causal attribution to one phase.
No separate absolute survival benefit is assigned to three adjuvant carboplatin/FU cycles.

00417.title: Cetuximab + cisplatin + fluorouracil · 21-day cycle
00417.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
00417.purpose: Cetuximab with cisplatin and fluorouracil is used to treat squamous head and neck cancer. Discuss the individual aim, likely benefit, symptom control and alternatives with your oncology team.
00417.schedule: Cisplatin is given on Day 1, fluorouracil on Days 1–4, and cetuximab on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 21-day cycle, for up to 6 combination cycles. The team may then consider weekly cetuximab alone under a separate maintenance plan (NCCP 00207). This is not an automatic continuation.
material_risks: Low blood counts, serious infection/sepsis and bleeding
Cetuximab skin/nail toxicity, electrolyte loss and severe infusion reactions
Fluorouracil mucositis/diarrhoea, hand-foot syndrome and cardiac/early excessive toxicity
Cisplatin kidney injury, hearing loss and persistent neuropathy
Potentially serious lung toxicity; fertility and reproductive effects
00417.discussion: Discuss intended benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or lasting harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Confirm the exact indication and current licensed/off-label position.
limitations: Not a comparison with modern immunotherapy or proof of benefit for all locally advanced settings.
Do not assign the pooled result separately to cisplatin-only or carboplatin-only patients.
support: Give an antihistamine and a corticosteroid at least one hour before cetuximab; continue this premedication at subsequent doses. Reconcile steroids with any antiemetic prescription to avoid duplication.
Ask specifically about earlier antibody reactions, red-meat allergy, tick bites and any cetuximab IgE result. Premedication does not eliminate severe or delayed reactions.
Use a local EGFR-inhibitor skin plan, moisturiser and sun protection; assess painful, infected or intolerable rash and nail changes promptly.

NCCP allows observation to cease after two reaction-free cetuximab doses, whereas current Erbitux SmPC section 4.2 requires monitoring during and for at least one hour after each infusion. Agree and document the governed observation plan; do not automatically remove observation.

00696.title: Paclitaxel Days 1, 8, 15 + cetuximab Days 1, 15 · 28-day cycle
00696.setting: Recurrent and/or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma under NCCP 00696.
00696.purpose: Paclitaxel and cetuximab aim to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread and may help symptoms. Your team explains expected benefit, uncertainty and options in light of your previous treatment.
00696.schedule: Paclitaxel is given on Days 1, 8 and 15, with cetuximab on Days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. There is no scheduled treatment dose on Day 22. Both medicines continue while appropriate, until progression or unacceptable side effects; the protocol does not set a fixed total number of cycles.
material_risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, fatigue and hair loss
Peripheral neuropathy which may persist; muscle/joint pain
Cetuximab skin/nail toxicity and electrolyte loss
Immediate or delayed infusion allergy despite premedication
Mouth/bowel inflammation and potentially serious lung toxicity; reproductive effects
00696.discussion: Discuss intended benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or lasting harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Explain and document the off-label indication/combination and current licensing position under local policy.
limitations: Small non-randomised selected cohort; different default paclitaxel dose and prior-therapy requirements.
The corrigendum corrects grade 1/2 paronychia to 12/35 (34%); it does not change efficacy.
support: Give an antihistamine and a corticosteroid at least one hour before cetuximab; continue this premedication at subsequent doses. Reconcile steroids with any antiemetic prescription to avoid duplication.
Ask specifically about earlier antibody reactions, red-meat allergy, tick bites and any cetuximab IgE result. Premedication does not eliminate severe or delayed reactions.
Use a local EGFR-inhibitor skin plan, moisturiser and sun protection; assess painful, infected or intolerable rash and nail changes promptly.

NCCP allows observation to cease after two reaction-free cetuximab doses, whereas current Erbitux SmPC section 4.2 requires monitoring during and for at least one hour after each infusion. Agree and document the governed observation plan; do not automatically remove observation.
Arrange nutrition, weight and swallowing review early. Dietitian and speech and language therapy input should follow the person’s needs; swallowing safety cannot be inferred from a general leaflet.
Use the agreed mouth-care and dental plan. Report painful swallowing, mouth ulceration, weight loss or inability to drink before the next appointment.
Reconcile prescription, over-the-counter and complementary medicines. Discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding using the actual products and individual circumstances.
Confirm the hospital’s urgent contact and fever instructions. Infection, bleeding, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, chest pain or new breathlessness need prompt assessment, not the next routine review.
Consider prescribed analgesia for paclitaxel-related muscle/joint pain. Assess neuropathy before it becomes disabling; do not wait for a routine cycle boundary.

Both medicines are low emetic risk in NCCP v2; do not carry forward an unsupported moderate-risk antiemetic schedule. Day 1/15 cetuximab steroid/antihistamine premedication also covers paclitaxel; Day 8 needs its distinct plan.
